Five ads ran in the first ~35 hours. Total spend was $124.70. Link clicks ranged from 3 to 16. Downloads were sparse: only one per ad, mostly view-through.

Each ad line item has a $18.75 daily budget. The first 35 hours cost roughly $25 per ad, slightly under the expected $27.34 pace across eight days. Installations are tracked as DOWNLOAD events, and only three installs have occurred so far.

CPA and CPC vary sharply across ads. The iPhone US CA line had the best click volume and produced the only click-attributed install at $24.96 CPA. The bright planet ad cost $24.98 CPA. The Perseids ad had the worst CTR at $8.32 CPC. Point and name and free $0 ads generated clicks but zero installs. Three conversions in roughly 35 hours is too early to pause any line.

View-through installs are noisy because they lack a strict one-day window. Link clicks are the stronger leading signal. The iPhone US CA ad leads with 16 clicks and one install. The bright planet ad follows with 11 clicks and one install. Point and name and free $0 ads generated clicks but zero installs. Perseids has only three clicks and one view install, with a CTR roughly five times lower than the iPhone post.

Perseids should not be paused yet. The iPhone US CA ad is the best click-through performer and produced the only click-attributed install. Its copy better targets iPhone users in the US and Canada. The budget should shift toward this line.

Bright planet and point and name will stay in the rotation. Perseids should be paused or reduced; its CTR is five times worse than the iPhone US CA line, and three clicks after $25 spent is a poor trajectory. The free $0 ad is middle-weak but acceptable to keep for now.

Pausing Perseids now would free roughly $125 in remaining budget. The ad has spent about $25 of its $150 total budget. Its view-through install is likely a coincidence given 21,000 impressions. The iPhone post's click-attributed install is the stronger signal.

Perseids will be paused and its remaining budget reallocated to the iPhone US CA and bright planet ads. The total campaign cap stays at $750. Perseids will be capped at roughly $25 to stop further spending, then its budget can be moved.

Perseids will be capped at $25 to freeze its remaining budget. The iPhone US CA ad will receive the extra $125, raising its total budget to $275 and its daily spend to about $38. That leaves roughly six and a half days before the campaign ends.
